plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.7.13
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to use Pappus' Theorem to find the volume of the torus generated by revolving a circular region of radius b about an axis at distance a from the center of the circle. The figure shows a 3D torus in perspective with the vertical axis of revolution passing through its central hole; the distance a from the axis to the center of the circular cross-section and the radius b of the cross-section are labeled, with the cross-section highlighted as a small circle on the right side of the torus. A red dashed ellipse traces the circular path traveled by the centroid, with direction arrows, and a caption box reads The centroid travels a distance 2pi a. The figure shows that by Pappus' Theorem the volume V = (2 pi a)(pi b^2) = 2 pi^2 a b^2, since the centroid traverses a full circle of circumference 2 pi a as the region revolves.

elements: Grey shaded torus (major radius a, tube radius b) centered on origin, lying in the horizontal plane, viewed from ~28° above
Vertical black axis of revolution through the center of the hole, extending above and below the torus
Black dot marking the center point where the axis meets the torus mid-plane
Red dashed circle (drawn as an ellipse in this view) through the tube centers — the centroid path of radius a
Two red arrowheads on the dashed path indicating direction of revolution (one on far side pointing right, one on near side pointing left)
Blue-outlined generating circle of radius b filled pale orange, standing in the vertical plane on the right side of the torus (cross-section of the tube)
Red dot at the center of the generating circle marking the centroid of the region
Horizontal double-headed black arrow from the axis dot to the red centroid dot, labeled 'a'
Short horizontal double-headed black arrow from the centroid to the outer edge of the generating circle, labeled 'b'
Pale-orange caption callout box with arrow pointing at the near side of the torus: 'The centroid travels a distance 2πa.'
Readout of Pappus results: V = (2πa)(πb²) = 2π²ab² and S = (2πa)(2πb) = 4π²ab

interactions.label: a (axis to centroid)
interactions.teaches: Volume and surface area scale linearly with the distance the centroid travels, 2πa

interactions.label: b (cross-section radius)
interactions.teaches: Volume grows with b² (the region's area πb²) while surface area grows only with b (its perimeter 2πb)

interactions.label: Revolve generating circle
interactions.teaches: The torus is swept out by one circular region revolving about the axis, its centroid tracing a circle of length 2πa

interactions.label: Pappus components
interactions.teaches: Each factor in V = (2πa)(πb²) corresponds to a specific piece of the picture: the path length and the region's area
The dashed red ellipse is really a circle in the horizontal plane, and the generating circle stands perpendicular to it

demo_steps.title: The figure as drawn
demo_steps.narration: A torus with its vertical axis of revolution; the red dashed circle is the path of the centroid at distance a, and the blue circle of radius b is the region being revolved.

demo_steps.title: The revolving region
demo_steps.narration: Only the pale orange disk of radius b remains: a plane region of area πb² standing perpendicular to the path.

demo_steps.title: Sweeping out the solid
demo_steps.narration: Play the revolution: the disk turns a full 360° about the axis and its centroid traces a circle of circumference 2πa.

demo_steps.title: Reading off a and b
demo_steps.narration: The double arrow from the axis to the red centroid is a; the short arrow from centroid to rim is b. Change a and watch the hole open up.

demo_steps.title: Fatten the tube
demo_steps.narration: Increasing b enlarges the cross-sectional area πb²; volume responds quadratically while surface area responds only linearly.

demo_steps.title: Pappus' Theorem
demo_steps.narration: Multiply the travel distance by the area: V = (2πa)(πb²) = 2π²ab², and by the perimeter for S = 4π²ab.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units: default a = 2.0, b = 0.6, torus centered at origin in the XZ plane (horizontal), axis of revolution along +Y from y = -2.2 to y = +2.6 as a thin black line (radius ~0.015). Torus major radius a, tube radius b, so outer extent 2(a+b) ≈ 5.2 wide, height 2b. Black dot (radius 0.07) at origin. Red dashed circle of radius a in the y = 0 plane, drawn in screen projection as a wide flat ellipse (camera elevation ~28° makes its vertical semi-axis ≈ 0.47× horizontal). Two red cone arrowheads on the dashed circle at the far (+Z back) point pointing toward +X and the near (-Z front) point pointing toward -X, indicating counterclockwise-from-above revolution. Generating circle sits on the +X side at (a, 0, 0): a disk of radius b lying in the XY plane (normal along Z, i.e. facing the viewer), filled pale orange #F7D9A6 at ~0.75 opacity with a 3px light-blue outline #3FA9E0. Red dot #E8413A radius 0.06 at its center. Horizontal double-headed black arrow along +X from origin to (a,0,0) at y=0, label 'a' italic serif centered above it; short double-headed arrow from (a,0,0) to (a+b,0,0) labeled 'b' above it. Colors: torus light grey gradient #E9E9EB highlight to #A9AAAE shading (glossy, soft specular, lit from upper-left); dashed path red #E8413A, dash 0.12 / gap 0.10; axis and dimension arrows black #111; callout box fill #F4DDB0 with grey border #9A9A9A and a pointer arrow from its top-left toward the near rim of the torus, text in dark grey sans-serif 'The centroid travels a distance 2πa.' placed at lower-right of the frame. Formulas: V = (2πa)(πb²) = 2π²ab², S = (2πa)(2πb) = 4π²ab; require a > b for a proper hole — clamp b ≤ 0.9a.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the torus with THREE.TorusGeometry(a, b, 32, 96) rotated -π/2 about X so its hole axis is +Y; rebuild (or rescale) geometry on slider change. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial (roughness ~0.35, clearcoat) with a hemisphere light plus a key directional light from upper-left to reproduce the glossy grey shading. Dashed centroid circle: LineDashed (computeLineDistances) or a thin tube with alpha dashes so it stays visible over the torus; render it with depthTest on so the far half is hidden behind the tube, matching the source where the dashes disappear under the surface. For the sweep animation, draw a partial torus via TorusGeometry with thetaLength = progress·2π and move the generating disk to angle = progress, keeping the traced red arc length in sync; on loop completion show the full torus briefly. Labels 'a' and 'b' as CSS2DRenderer/sprite HTML in italic serif so they match the textbook; caption box as an HTML overlay anchored in the lower-right with an SVG pointer polygon. Arrowheads via ConeGeometry or ArrowHelper. Orbit constrained to polar 10°–80° so the figure is never seen edge-on from below.

authoredContext:
Use Pappus’ Theorem to find the volume V of the torus generated by revolving a circular region of radius b about a line at a distance a (greater than b) from the center of the circle (Figure 5.7.13). By symmetry, the centroid of a circular region is its center. Thus, the distance
traveled by the centroid is 2πa. Since the area of a circle of radius b is πb2, it follows from
Pappus’ Theorem that the volume of the torus is
V = (2πa)(πb2
) = 2π2
ab2

discrepancies: The red dashed centroid path with its two red arrowheads — the most distinctive annotation in the source — is not visible: it is drawn at radius a on the mid-plane, i.e. buried inside the opaque tube, so nothing of it appears in the default view (the source draws it overlaid on top of the torus).

The pale-orange generating region is likewise invisible in the default state: the disk of radius b sits exactly coincident with the torus cross-section, so it is occluded/z-fighting; only a thin arc of the blue outline pokes out on the right, whereas the source shows a fully visible orange filled circle with a complete blue rim.
The red centroid dot at distance a is not discernible, so the 'a' dimension arrow appears to terminate in empty space rather than at the centroid marker shown in the source.
The 'a' and 'b' italic labels are rendered very small and low-contrast over the torus, far from the prominent serif italic labels in the source.
The caption callout box ('The centroid travels a distance 2πa.') is rendered at a tiny scale far below the figure and is effectively unreadable, versus the large prominent callout in the source.
The axis line is much shorter/thinner relative to the torus than in the source, where it extends well above and below the ring.
evaluation.notes: Correct torus/axis/dimension geometry and a rich, conceptually sound set of interactions (a/b sliders, revolve animation, component isolation, guided steps), but the two signature red dashed centroid path and orange generating region are hidden inside the opaque torus in the default view and the a/b labels and caption callout are far too small, so the default render reads as a plain grey donut rather than the source figure.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (concept_accuracy 5); the problems are rendering-level — occluded centroid path and generating disk due to depth/opacity and coincident geometry, plus undersized labels and caption — which are concrete implementation fixes.

plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.7.13
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to use Pappus' Theorem to find the volume of the torus generated by revolving a circular region of radius b about an axis at distance a from the center of the circle. The figure shows a 3D torus in perspective with the vertical axis of revolution passing through its central hole; the distance a from the axis to the center of the circular cross-section and the radius b of the cross-section are labeled, with the cross-section highlighted as a small circle on the right side of the torus. A red dashed ellipse traces the circular path traveled by the centroid, with direction arrows, and a caption box reads The centroid travels a distance 2pi a. The figure shows that by Pappus' Theorem the volume V = (2 pi a)(pi b^2) = 2 pi^2 a b^2, since the centroid traverses a full circle of circumference 2 pi a as the region revolves.

elements: Grey shaded torus (major radius a, tube radius b) centered on origin, lying in the horizontal plane, viewed from ~28° above
Vertical black axis of revolution through the center of the hole, extending above and below the torus
Black dot marking the center point where the axis meets the torus mid-plane
Red dashed circle (drawn as an ellipse in this view) through the tube centers — the centroid path of radius a
Two red arrowheads on the dashed path indicating direction of revolution (one on far side pointing right, one on near side pointing left)
Blue-outlined generating circle of radius b filled pale orange, standing in the vertical plane on the right side of the torus (cross-section of the tube)
Red dot at the center of the generating circle marking the centroid of the region
Horizontal double-headed black arrow from the axis dot to the red centroid dot, labeled 'a'
Short horizontal double-headed black arrow from the centroid to the outer edge of the generating circle, labeled 'b'
Pale-orange caption callout box with arrow pointing at the near side of the torus: 'The centroid travels a distance 2πa.'
Readout of Pappus results: V = (2πa)(πb²) = 2π²ab² and S = (2πa)(2πb) = 4π²ab

interactions.label: a (axis to centroid)
interactions.teaches: Volume and surface area scale linearly with the distance the centroid travels, 2πa

interactions.label: b (cross-section radius)
interactions.teaches: Volume grows with b² (the region's area πb²) while surface area grows only with b (its perimeter 2πb)

interactions.label: Revolve generating circle
interactions.teaches: The torus is swept out by one circular region revolving about the axis, its centroid tracing a circle of length 2πa

interactions.label: Pappus components
interactions.teaches: Each factor in V = (2πa)(πb²) corresponds to a specific piece of the picture: the path length and the region's area
The dashed red ellipse is really a circle in the horizontal plane, and the generating circle stands perpendicular to it

demo_steps.title: The figure as drawn
demo_steps.narration: A torus with its vertical axis of revolution; the red dashed circle is the path of the centroid at distance a, and the blue circle of radius b is the region being revolved.

demo_steps.title: The revolving region
demo_steps.narration: Only the pale orange disk of radius b remains: a plane region of area πb² standing perpendicular to the path.

demo_steps.title: Sweeping out the solid
demo_steps.narration: Play the revolution: the disk turns a full 360° about the axis and its centroid traces a circle of circumference 2πa.

demo_steps.title: Reading off a and b
demo_steps.narration: The double arrow from the axis to the red centroid is a; the short arrow from centroid to rim is b. Change a and watch the hole open up.

demo_steps.title: Fatten the tube
demo_steps.narration: Increasing b enlarges the cross-sectional area πb²; volume responds quadratically while surface area responds only linearly.

demo_steps.title: Pappus' Theorem
demo_steps.narration: Multiply the travel distance by the area: V = (2πa)(πb²) = 2π²ab², and by the perimeter for S = 4π²ab.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units: default a = 2.0, b = 0.6, torus centered at origin in the XZ plane (horizontal), axis of revolution along +Y from y = -2.2 to y = +2.6 as a thin black line (radius ~0.015). Torus major radius a, tube radius b, so outer extent 2(a+b) ≈ 5.2 wide, height 2b. Black dot (radius 0.07) at origin. Red dashed circle of radius a in the y = 0 plane, drawn in screen projection as a wide flat ellipse (camera elevation ~28° makes its vertical semi-axis ≈ 0.47× horizontal). Two red cone arrowheads on the dashed circle at the far (+Z back) point pointing toward +X and the near (-Z front) point pointing toward -X, indicating counterclockwise-from-above revolution. Generating circle sits on the +X side at (a, 0, 0): a disk of radius b lying in the XY plane (normal along Z, i.e. facing the viewer), filled pale orange #F7D9A6 at ~0.75 opacity with a 3px light-blue outline #3FA9E0. Red dot #E8413A radius 0.06 at its center. Horizontal double-headed black arrow along +X from origin to (a,0,0) at y=0, label 'a' italic serif centered above it; short double-headed arrow from (a,0,0) to (a+b,0,0) labeled 'b' above it. Colors: torus light grey gradient #E9E9EB highlight to #A9AAAE shading (glossy, soft specular, lit from upper-left); dashed path red #E8413A, dash 0.12 / gap 0.10; axis and dimension arrows black #111; callout box fill #F4DDB0 with grey border #9A9A9A and a pointer arrow from its top-left toward the near rim of the torus, text in dark grey sans-serif 'The centroid travels a distance 2πa.' placed at lower-right of the frame. Formulas: V = (2πa)(πb²) = 2π²ab², S = (2πa)(2πb) = 4π²ab; require a > b for a proper hole — clamp b ≤ 0.9a.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the torus with THREE.TorusGeometry(a, b, 32, 96) rotated -π/2 about X so its hole axis is +Y; rebuild (or rescale) geometry on slider change. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial (roughness ~0.35, clearcoat) with a hemisphere light plus a key directional light from upper-left to reproduce the glossy grey shading. Dashed centroid circle: LineDashed (computeLineDistances) or a thin tube with alpha dashes so it stays visible over the torus; render it with depthTest on so the far half is hidden behind the tube, matching the source where the dashes disappear under the surface. For the sweep animation, draw a partial torus via TorusGeometry with thetaLength = progress·2π and move the generating disk to angle = progress, keeping the traced red arc length in sync; on loop completion show the full torus briefly. Labels 'a' and 'b' as CSS2DRenderer/sprite HTML in italic serif so they match the textbook; caption box as an HTML overlay anchored in the lower-right with an SVG pointer polygon. Arrowheads via ConeGeometry or ArrowHelper. Orbit constrained to polar 10°–80° so the figure is never seen edge-on from below.
